quote: Democritus imagined this 2,400 years ago, and there was a time, roughly 1803–1922, when Science thought he was right.
content: The dates bracket Dalton and (presumably) the Compton effect or the Bohr–Kramers–Slater episode, and they are too generous at both ends. Chemists were not agreed that atoms were physically real until Perrin’s Brownian-motion measurements around 1908 (Ostwald and Mach held out until then), and the billiard-ball picture was already dead by 1911, when Rutherford’s scattering showed the atom to be almost entirely empty space around a nucleus, following Thomson’s electron in 1897. Democritus’s atoms, moreover, had shapes and hooks, came in infinitely many kinds, and moved in a void that his critics denied could exist; the eighteenth-century Newtonian atom was a point centre of force (Boscovich, 1758), not a ball. There is no period in which physicists believed in Democritus’s atoms, and the “little billiard balls” of the essay are the popular image, not a stage of the science. The point matters because the essay’s argument is that the reader’s picture of atoms is naive; the essay’s picture of the history of atoms is the same picture, dated.

quote: But an Artificial Intelligence programmer who knows how to create a chess-playing program out of base matter has taken a genuine step toward crossing the gap. If you understand concepts like consequentialism, backward chaining, utility functions, and search trees, you can make merely causal/mechanical systems compute plans.
content: Anger is not planning, and the essay’s bridge crosses a different river. What the affective neuroscience of aggression describes is an evolved, fast, subcortical response: optogenetic stimulation of a hypothalamic nucleus produces attack behaviour in mice within seconds, and silencing it abolishes attack (Lin et al. (2011)); Panksepp’s RAGE system is an affect program with its own circuitry, not a utility function fed into minimax. The long-term plot with the scorpions is planning in the service of anger, and the essay’s worked example (Deep Blue’s search) is a model of the plot, not of the emotion that motivates it. So the “genuine step across the gap” is a step across the gap between billiard balls and plans, which the good-old-fashioned AI tradition had crossed by 1960; the gap the essay names, between billiard balls and “Grrr! Aaarg!”, is left where it was. The line “the billiard balls in the alcohol push on the billiard balls making up the utility function” is a picture of the wrong mechanism: alcohol’s effect on aggression runs through disinhibition of prefrontal control over the subcortical systems (Steele & Josephs (1990)), which is the opposite of a change to the utility function.

quote: Going from material substances that bend and break, burn and fall, push and shove, to angry behavior, is just a practice problem by the standards of modern philosophy. But it is an important practice problem. It can only be fully appreciated, if you realize how hard it would have been to solve before writing was invented. There was once an explanatory gap here—though it may not seem that way in hindsight, now that it’s been bridged for generations.
content: It has not been bridged, in the sense the essay means, for any animal. The one nervous system whose complete wiring diagram is known, the 302 neurons of C. elegans, mapped in 1986, has not yielded a prediction of the worm’s behaviour from the connectome, and the leaders of the field wrote a review explaining why: the map omits neuromodulation, gap-junction dynamics and the state-dependence that determine what the circuit does (Bargmann & Marder (2013)). For a human act of anger, no chain from molecules to the raised fist exists in any laboratory; what exists is the general confidence, well founded, that such a chain would be found, plus a set of intermediate-level findings about circuits and neurotransmitters. The essay’s “bridged” means “we are confident it is bridgeable,” which is a different claim, and it is the claim that Zombies! Zombies? will later call “not-quite-faith-based reductionism.” The explanatory gap was not crossed by Deep Blue; it was declared crossable by analogy with Deep Blue, and the analogy was drawn to the wrong phenomenon.
